newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Pakistani cricket player to face rape charges.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cricket player to face rape charges.

text.p: An 18-year-old Pakistani cricket player will go on trial on Tuesday to face charges of raping a woman tourist at a hotel where his team was staying.
Zeeshan Pervez, a member of Pakistan's Under-19 team, which is now playing the West Indies in Barbados, has been free on bail since his arrest on Sept. 1 for the alleged incident.
Magistrate Martin Gayle ruled on Friday there was sufficient evidence for the case to go to trial, although he noted several inconsistencies in the prosecution's case.
A 36-year-old Jamaican national who has lived in Boston for the past 18 years alleged that Pervez entered her hotel room late on Aug. 31.

The woman told police Pervez, who was also staying at the hotel while the cricket team played a four-day match in Jamaica, offered two of her three children his towels so they could go to the swimming pool.

The two children left their three-year-old sibling asleep in the room with Pervez and their mother. The children told police that when they returned 30 minutes later they found their mother on the telephone, crying and claiming she had been raped.
Prosecution witness Dr. Herb Elliott told the court he examined the woman, and while he found evidence of sexual intercourse, there were no injuries.
Pervez claimed the couple had consensual sex.
